problem: Section 1 lists the five components as message, sender, receiver, medium and protocol and says 'The five parts are drawn as a chain in the figure below'. The figure is titled 'Five components of data communication' but its five boxes are source, modem, medium, modem, server. There is no message box and no protocol box, so the figure names a different set of five from the text. A student revising from the figure will list the wrong five.
fix: Retitle the figure 'Source, transmitter, medium, receiver and destination' (or 'The sender–transmitter–medium–receiver–destination chain') and change the sentence in Section 1 to: 'Inside the sender and receiver the chain splits further: a transmitter (modem or network card) puts the bits on the medium and a receiver takes them off. The figure shows that chain, with the message and the protocol sitting above it.'

problem: 'Mobile networks already switch between half-duplex and full-duplex operation in time division duplex (TDD) bands' is wrong. A TDD band uses one frequency and alternates the direction in time, so it does not become full-duplex. Uplink and downlink speeds differ because the frame gives each direction a different share of time slots, not because the link switches to full duplex.
fix: 'Mobile networks in time division duplex (TDD) bands use one frequency and take turns, sending downlink and uplink in different time slots, so the link works like a half-duplex line. Uplink and downlink speeds differ because the frame gives each direction a different share of slots. Frequency division duplex (FDD) uses two separate frequencies and can run both directions at once.'

problem: 'Simplex works only when the protocol is right in advance' is vague; 'right' does not say what must be right.
fix: 'Simplex works only when the protocol is fixed in advance, because the receiver has no way to ask for a repeat.'

problem: 'A server pushes a bank statement that your app can only read' suggests the phone sends nothing at all, yet the app had to request the statement. The example hides the request and can mislead a student about what simplex means here.
fix: 'A server streams a bank statement that your app only displays: the statement data itself moves one way, and the app never sends anything back on that stream.'
